title: Signal boarding pass and late-stage instrumentation notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact 'boarding pass' for late-stage instrumentation and dashboard signoff ahead of rollouts. Intended for engineers finishing feature rollouts, SREs who own runbooks, and product managers coordinating visibility. The goal is a lightweight checklist and explicit metric/tracing contracts so we can flip a feature flag and have acceptable investigative coverage without over-indexing on metric volume.

Context / when to use this: 
- After the feature-level metrics and traces are implemented but before running canaries.
- When a product is >70% through QA and we need operational signals for rollout gating.
- For fast-moving model rollouts where telemetry budgets are constrained (quantized model experiments, dedicated pool rollouts).

High-level rules (quick):
- Minimal signal set first: 6–10 probes per feature (3 core SLO signals, 2 health probes, 1 cost/telemetry check, optional quality probe).
- Prefer cheap synthetic probes for early detection (latency, simple prompt repro, prefix-warmth check).
- Trace anchors for every customer-facing code path (span for request entry, routing decision, model inference, fallback). Span depth should be shallow (3–6 spans) to control trace cost.
- Always include a canonical request-id and tenant tags on spans/metrics.
- Dashboard tiles should be actionable: include a playbook link and top-3 drilldowns in the tile description.

Boarding-pass checklist (flip when all true):
- [ ] Metrics: SLO/SLI candidates defined with owners and aggregation windows.
- [ ] Traces: path-level spans instrumented and sampled (sample policy specified).
- [ ] Dashboards: 5 default tiles created (overview, latency quantiles, error-rate, kv-cache warmth, cost-per-token).
- [ ] Runbook links wired to dashboard tile descriptions and the alert.
- [ ] Synthetic probes scheduled (hourly for canary, 5m for production post-rollout).
- [ ] Alert thresholds proposed and reviewed with SRE.
- [ ] Query cost estimate <= telemetry budget for the feature (see Cost estimate section).

Metric definitions (minimal table in text):
- request.count: owner=feature-eng, unit=ops/min, agg=sum over 1m, alert if sustained drop >50% for 5m (indicates routing or upstream issue).
- request.first_token_latency_ms: owner=sre, unit=ms, agg=p95 over 5m, alert if p95 > 2x baseline for 10m.
- inference.token_emit_rate: owner=runtime, unit=tokens/s, agg=median over 1m, used for capacity alarms.
- kvcache.warmth_percent: owner=serving-runtime, unit=percent, agg=avg over 5m, alert if < 10% for high-tail models.
- assistant.quality_flag_rate: owner=ml-quality, unit=flags per 1k requests, agg=rate over 1h, triggers manual review workflow.
- telemetry.query_cost_estimate: owner=observability, unit=$/hour, agg=sum over 1h, must be below budget.

Trace conventions (to keep consistent and compact):
- Root span name: featureName.request (e.g., chat-completions.request)
- Child spans: router.select_model, runtime.kv_lookup, runtime.infer, runtime.quantize-step (optional), output.postprocess
- Important attributes (tags): tenant.id, request.id, model.version, route.policy, kv.hit (boolean), seq_len
- Sampling: default 1% for production, 10% for canary; increase to 100% during incident windows via sampling override header.
- Span size guidance: avoid logging full prompt text in spans; store prompt hashes and a safe truncated summary (if PII safe).

Dashboard tile templates (one-line recipes):
- Overview tile: timeseries of request.count (1m) with p50/p95 latency overlays; title must include playbook link.
- Latency heatmap: bucketed by request.first_token_latency_ms percentiles; axis: time vs quantile; use color for severity.
- KV-warmth panel: single stat with sparkline + top tenants by warmth (table) for quick tenant triage.
- Error breakdown: stacked bar by error.code and template of top-5 failing prompts (prompt hash only).
- Cost slider: telemetry.query_cost_estimate with projected 24h cost and annotated commit/PR that added heavy queries.

Runbook & alerts (distilled):
- Alert priorities: P0 service-down, P1 SLO breach approaching budget, P2 cost anomaly or increasing trace volume.
- Immediate first steps for latency SLO breach: check kv-warmth, check model version rollout, check runtime token_emit_rate, compare to canary lanes.
- For quality regressions: route a small proportion to human-in-the-loop review and enable debug trace sampling header to 50% for affected tenants.

Telemetry cost estimate (quick calc):
- Count of dashboard queries x avg query cost + trace retention cost x estimated trace volume.
- Quick rule: keep panel count under 12 for feature-specific dashboard and sampling <= 1% by default.
- Example estimate: 5 tiles + 2 tables -> ~0.02 USD/hour in our cost model for low-cardinality signals; if adding high-cardinality top-tenants table multiply by 5.

Implementation notes (practical):
- Use existing metric names and tag schema (tenant, model, env) — avoid ad-hoc tags to prevent cardinality explosion.
- Prefer summary metrics (percentiles + counters) rather than logging raw values.
- If adding a trace attribute that increases cardinality (e.g., prompt-type), prefix with "lowcard_" and confirm with telemetry steward.
- Add a short description block at top of dashboard JSON with owner, ticket links, and rollback contact.

Owner signoff fields (fill before flip):
- Feature eng owner: ____________________
- SRE owner: ____________________
- Product owner: ____________________
- Telemetry steward review: ____________________

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Should we include end-user perceived latency metric (time-to-visible) and how to compute cheaply? (Action: Miguel to prototype synthetic browser timing probe).
- Confirm acceptable retention for canary traces (30d?) vs production (7d) per cost target. (Action: Leah to sync with cost team).
- Decide threshold for automatic sampling override during P0 incidents. (Action: SRE oncall to propose).

References and quick links:
- Confluence: OBS-boarding-pass (design doc)
- Jira: OBS-3456 (instrumentation epic)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/428 (dashboard tiles + alert rules)
- Slack: #obs-instrumentation (Mar 2025 thread)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact — the aim is to avoid creating a sprawling metric set. Look for opportunities to consolidate panels and reuse existing signals (search for metric prefixes request.*, runtime.*, kvcache.*).
- If you add a metric, add an owner and a cost estimate line in the PR description.

End.
